$comment: A 555 monostable on a battery_pack (5 V, 2 ohm, 22 uF across the rail): R = 100 kohm from the rail to pin 7 (tied to THR), C = 1 uF, TRIG pulled up to the rail by 1 kohm with a push_button to ground, OUT into 1 kohm. 0.4 s; the button is pressed at 0.2 s and released at 0.25 s (host stops of 100 us, 1 ms and 1/60 s all land on both).

Judged under ruling R122 (a), the handBound marker below: the core against these hand values within the stated bound; classic's distance from them is a divergence row, not a gate (circuit class '555 on a cell's rail': core/README.md, 'The 555 period on a moving rail'). test/core/battery-555-corpus.test.ts also runs the board on both engines at host stops of 100 us, 1 ms and 1/60 s.
By hand, the pulse is C charging from empty to 2u/3 through R, a ratio that does not depend on the rail: ln 3 R C = 109.8612 ms (the textbook 1.1 R C is 110 ms, 0.13 % long).
Power-on: OUT starts high and C starts empty, so the first pulse is the same 109.8612 ms: OUT falls at 109.8612 ms. DIS discharges C in 10 ohm x 1 uF, 10 us.

The press at 0.2 s takes TRIG to about 0 V (the contact's 1 mohm against 1 kohm): below u/3, so OUT rises at 0.2 s. It is released at 0.25 s, with the pulse running, and changes nothing. OUT falls at 0.2 + 109.8612 ms = 309.8612 ms. Edges in 0.4 s: rise at 0.2, falls at 109.8612 ms and 309.8612 ms.
Rail: 2 ohm in the pack, the 555's idle draw (about 5 mA) and the charge current move it by about 10 mV; the bound used by the test is 0.25 % of the edge's time + 5 us.

The rail capacitor's published current is not judged and not excused: the core publishes 0 for a capacitor directly across a battery's rail (publish_fixed_pair_capacitors, core/src/solve/mod.rs), classic C dv/dt (CORPUS follow-up; fix in progress). The report lists it as a known failing reading.

handBound.justification: The hand model holds the rail steady; the rail is not. The pack's 2 ohm carries a draw that changes with OUT's level (about 5 mA idle, then the charge current), so the rail moves about 10 mV between the phases (0.2 %) and the thresholds, which are fractions of the rail, move with it. That shifts an edge by about that fraction of its time (measured worst 0.04 % on the second pulse); 0.25 % covers it with margin, and 5 us covers the rail capacitor's own settling (2 ohm x 22 uF = 44 us). Classic is judged against the same values and its distance is recorded in the entry's divergence rows, at the app's 1/60 s stops, in numbers: 77 an edge up to 1.4 ms off, a rise lost in 100 ms; 78 up to 1.6 ms, a final count of 8 against 9; 79 a pulse end 0.56 ms late (a step-limited crossing search). So the bound is not set to admit classic.
